diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ be nonzero, $m\geq n$, and $\Vert A\Vert^{-1}A=U^\top V$ be the decomposition given in Lemma \ref{lem:orthogonal_decomposition}.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem normalizes A by its spectral norm. The critical values of MA(\tilde P,\tilde Q) correspond to σ/||A||, not σ. The remark omits the scaling factor ||A||, so arccos(σ) may be undefined or incorrect when ||A||≠1.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, $\sigma$ is a $(P,Q)$-singular value of $A$ if and only if $\arccos(\sigma)$ is a critical angle between $\wt P$ and $\wt Q$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change arccos(σ) to arccos(σ/||A||) or restrict to ||A||=1.
issues.overall_effect: Misstates the relationship between singular values of A and critical angles; only affects the remark, not the main theorem.
issues.title: Incorrect scaling in critical angle correspondence
issues.why_classification: Isolated misstatement in a remark, easily corrected, no downstream results depend on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
we define the \textit{Nash pairs} $(u^*, v^*)\in P\times Q$ of the problem $\SV(A,P,Q)$ as the unit vectors such that
\[
\langle u, A v^*\rangle \ge \langle u^*, A v^*\rangle, \qquad \langle u^*, A v\rangle \ge \langle u^*, A v^*\rangle, \qquad \forall\, (u, v)\in P\times Q : \|u\| = \|v\| = 1.
\]

issues.failure_explanation: A local minimum of the joint problem need not be a global minimizer in each block. Counterexample: P=Q=R^2_+, A=[[1,2],[2,1]]. The point u=(1,0), v=(0,1) is a local minimum (value 2) but for fixed v=(0,1), the subproblem in u is minimized at u=(0,1) with value 1, so it is not a Nash pair.

failure_location.quote: Observe also that any solution pair and all local minima of $\SV(A,P,Q)$ are Nash pairs.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove "and all local minima" or replace with "any solution pair is a Nash pair".
issues.overall_effect: The false statement is not used in the main proofs (only solution pairs being Nash pairs is used), but it is an incorrect mathematical observation.
issues.title: False claim that all local minima are Nash pairs
issues.why_classification: Isolated false observation, easily removed, no substantive result depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose that $G^\top A H$ is a nonnegative matrix. Then, there exists a solution pair $(u,v)$ of $\SV(A,P,Q)$ where $u$ and $v$ are generators of $P$ and $Q$, respectively, and the optimal value of $\SV(A,P,Q)$ is the minimum entry of $G^\top A H$.

issues.failure_explanation: The condition is necessary but not sufficient. Even if P and Q are single rays and G^T A H≥0, the value <u,Av> equals the scalar G^T A H, which need not equal ||A||. For example, P=Q=ray(e1), A=diag(0.5,2) gives ||A||=2 but <u,Av>=0.5.

failure_location.quote: However, the case $\langle u, Av\rangle =    \|A\|$ is easy to check, since it is equivalent to say that both $P,Q$ have only one generator and $G^\top AH$ is a $1\times 1$ nonnegative matrix.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace with the condition that <g,h> = ||A|| for the single generators, or check λ*=||A|| directly.
issues.overall_effect: The stated easy check for the case λ*=||A|| is incorrect; could mislead preprocessing.
issues.title: Incorrect condition for optimal value equal to ||A||
issues.why_classification: Local false claim about a boundary case, easily corrected, not central to the algorithms.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let  $A_x:=\ol H^+ A^\top\ol G$,  $A_y:=\ol G^+ A \ol H$
$M := \begin{pmatrix} 0& \ol H^+ A^\top\ol G\\\ol G^+ A\ol H& 0  \end{pmatrix}$

issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm defines A_y and A_x with A and A^T swapped compared to the correct definitions in Proposition pro:sufficient_conditions_feasibility and Theorem th:critical_points_SVcones. As written, the algorithm constructs the matrix M for the transposed problem SV(A^T,P,Q), so it may miss the correct optimal solution when A is not symmetric and the optimal support has size >2.

failure_location.quote: \State $ A_y = \ol G^+ A^\top \ol H$, $A_x = \ol H^+A \ol G$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Swap A and A^T in the definitions of A_x and A_y in Algorithm alg:active_set to match Proposition pro:sufficient_conditions_feasibility.
issues.overall_effect: The exactness guarantee of BFAS (Algorithm alg:active_set) fails as written for non-symmetric A.
issues.title: BFAS algorithm uses transposed matrices in A_x and A_y
issues.why_classification: A short, local correction (swap A and A^T) restores the algorithm's exactness without changing the method or guarantees.
